title: Church history, 1847–2026
reviewed: 2026-10-18. Each quote was copied from the linked article and is checked by npm run verify:sources.

events.title: The pioneers reach the Salt Lake Valley
events.summary: Brigham Young's vanguard company arrives after crossing the plains. Settlement of the valley begins.

source.quote: In July 1847, the first company reached the Salt Lake Valley

events.title: The first Sunday School in the valley
events.summary: Richard Ballantyne holds the first formal Sunday School of the Church in Salt Lake City.

source.quote: held on December 9, 1849, in Salt Lake City

events.title: The Deseret News is founded
events.summary: The first newspaper in Utah begins publication.

source.quote: Founded in 1850, it was the first newspaper to be published in Utah.

events.title: Congress creates Utah Territory
events.summary: The United States organizes the Territory of Utah. Brigham Young becomes its first governor.

source.quote: existed from September 9, 1850

events.title: The Pearl of Great Price is first published
events.summary: Franklin D. Richards publishes a pamphlet of Joseph Smith's writings for British members.

source.quote: Richards in Liverpool, England, in 1851

events.title: Plural marriage is announced publicly
events.summary: Orson Pratt publicly announces and defends the practice at Brigham Young's request.

source.quote: in 1852, Orson Pratt, a member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, publicly announced

events.title: The first missionaries reach Hong Kong
events.summary: Three missionaries sail to Hong Kong, an early mission far beyond Europe and America.

source.quote: In 1853, the LDS Church sent its first missionaries to Hong Kong

events.title: The handcart companies
events.summary: Emigrants pull handcarts across the plains to Utah. Two late companies are caught by snow in Wyoming.

source.quote: The Mormon handcart movement began in 1856 and continued until 1860.

events.title: The Utah War
events.summary: A United States army marches on Utah Territory. The standoff ends without a major battle.

source.quote: The confrontation lasted from May 1857 to July 1858.

events.title: The Mountain Meadows Massacre
events.summary: Latter-day Saint militiamen murder at least 120 members of the Baker–Fancher wagon train. It happens during the Utah War.

source.quote: (September 7–11, 1857)

events.title: The Salt Lake Tabernacle is built
events.summary: The Church builds a great domed hall for its meetings. It hosts general conference until 2000.

source.quote: The tabernacle was built from 1863 to 1875

events.title: The Young Women organization begins
events.summary: Brigham Young organizes a society for the young women of the Church.

source.quote: founded by LDS Church president Brigham Young in 1869

events.title: Brigham Young Academy is founded
events.summary: A school in Provo opens that later becomes Brigham Young University.

source.quote: It was founded in 1875 by religious leader Brigham Young

events.title: The St. George temple is completed
events.summary: The first temple completed in Utah opens in the southern settlements.

source.quote: this temple was completed in March 1877

events.title: Brigham Young dies
events.summary: The Church's second president dies after leading it for three decades.

source.quote: from 1847 until his death in 1877

events.title: The Primary is organized
events.summary: Aurelia Spencer Rogers organizes a weekly meeting to teach children.

source.quote: first organized in 1878 by Aurelia Spencer Rogers in Farmington, Utah

events.title: The Pearl of Great Price becomes scripture
events.summary: Church members accept the revised Pearl of Great Price as scripture.

source.quote: canonized in 1880

events.title: The Salt Lake Temple is dedicated
events.summary: After 40 years of building, the great granite temple is dedicated.

source.quote: Dedicated in 1893, it was constructed over a period of 40 years.

events.title: Utah becomes a state
events.summary: After agreeing to outlaw polygamy, Utah is admitted as the 45th state.

source.quote: in 1896, after it agreed to outlaw polygamy, it was admitted as the 45th

events.title: The Laie Hawaii Temple is dedicated
events.summary: A temple is dedicated in Hawaii, the first outside the continental United States.

source.quote: dedicating the completed structure on November 27, 1919

events.title: The Cardston Alberta Temple is dedicated
events.summary: A temple is dedicated in Canada among the Latter-day Saint settlements of southern Alberta.

source.quote: The temple was dedicated on August 26-29, 1923

events.title: The first temple in Europe
events.summary: David O. McKay dedicates a temple near Bern, Switzerland. It is the Church's first in Europe.

quote: the church's first temple in Europe

events.title: The first temple in the Southern Hemisphere
events.summary: A temple is completed near Hamilton, New Zealand.

source.quote: With its completion in 1958, it was the church's first temple in the Southern Hemisphere

events.title: The Washington D.C. Temple is dedicated
events.summary: A temple rises near the national capital, the first east of the Mississippi since Nauvoo.

source.quote: Since its dedication in 1974

events.title: The first temple in South America
events.summary: Spencer W. Kimball dedicates a temple in São Paulo, Brazil.

quote: the first Latter-day Saint temple built in South America

events.title: The first temple in Asia
events.summary: A temple is dedicated in Tokyo, Japan.

source.quote: dedicated in 1980, it was the first temple built in Asia

events.title: The Book of Mormon gains a subtitle
events.summary: The Church adds the subtitle “Another Testament of Jesus Christ” to its editions.

source.quote: In 1982, it added the subtitle

events.title: The Mexico City Temple is dedicated
events.summary: Gordon B. Hinckley dedicates a large temple in Mexico City.

source.quote: dedicated on December 2, 1983

events.title: The Manila Philippines Temple is dedicated
events.summary: A temple is dedicated for the fast-growing Church in the Philippines.

source.quote: dedicated in nine sessions from September 25 to 27, 1984

events.title: The first temple in Africa
events.summary: A temple is dedicated in South Africa. Temples now stand on every inhabited continent.

quote: the first temple built on the African continent

events.title: A temple in East Germany
events.summary: A temple is dedicated at Freiberg in Communist East Germany.

source.quote: the temple was dedicated on June 29 and June 30, 1985

events.title: The Seoul Korea Temple is dedicated
events.summary: Gordon B. Hinckley dedicates a temple in Seoul, South Korea.

source.quote: dedicated on December 14–15, 1985

events.title: The Family: A Proclamation to the World
events.summary: Gordon B. Hinckley reads a proclamation on marriage and family at a general meeting.

source.wiki: The Family: A Proclamation to the World
source.quote: first read the proclamation on September 23, 1995

events.title: The Hong Kong China Temple is dedicated
events.summary: A temple is dedicated in Hong Kong, a year before its return to China.

source.quote: On May 26–27, 1996, the temple was dedicated

events.title: The Living Christ
events.summary: The fifteen apostles sign a written testimony of Jesus Christ.

source.wiki: The Living Christ: The Testimony of the Apostles
source.quote: issued on January 1, 2000

events.title: The Conference Center opens
events.summary: A 21,000-seat hall replaces the Tabernacle for general conference.

source.quote: Completed in 2000, the 21,000-seat Conference Center

events.title: The Perpetual Education Fund
events.summary: The Church begins a loan fund for the education of young members in poorer countries.

source.quote: Hinckley on March 31, 2001

events.title: The Nauvoo temple is rebuilt
events.summary: A rebuilt temple is dedicated on the site of the original. The date marks Joseph Smith's death.

source.quote: dedicated by Hinckley on June 27, 2002

events.title: The Accra Ghana Temple is dedicated
events.summary: Gordon B. Hinckley dedicates the first temple in West Africa.

source.quote: dedicated by Hinckley on January 11, 2004

events.title: The Kyiv Ukraine Temple is dedicated
events.summary: Thomas S. Monson dedicates a temple in Ukraine, in the former Soviet Union.

source.quote: The temple was dedicated on 29 August 2010

events.title: The missionary age is lowered
events.summary: Thomas S. Monson announces that young men and women may serve missions earlier. Missionary numbers surge.

source.quote: until October 6, 2012

events.title: Russell M. Nelson leads the Church
events.summary: A former heart surgeon serves as the Church's seventeenth president until his death in 2025.

source.quote: from 2018 until his death in 2025

events.title: The Kinshasa temple is dedicated
events.summary: The first temple in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is dedicated.

source.wiki: Kinshasa Democratic Republic of the Congo Temple
source.quote: dedicated on April 14, 2019

events.title: The Rome Italy Temple is dedicated
events.summary: A temple opens in Rome after its dedication in 2019.

source.quote: opened after its dedication in 2019

events.title: Dallin H. Oaks becomes president
events.summary: After President Nelson's death, Dallin H. Oaks becomes the Church's eighteenth president.

source.quote: On October 14, 2025, Oaks was appointed as the church's eighteenth president
